title.zh: 小白兔的眼睛为什么是红的
title.en: Why Are White Rabbits’ Eyes Red?

content.zh: 小白兔身上的色素很少，眼睛里的血管就透了出来，看上去红红的。其实它的眼睛本来没有颜色，我们看到的是血的颜色。
content.en: White rabbits have almost no pigment, so the blood vessels in their eyes show through and look red. Their eyes are colourless; we are seeing the colour of blood.

imageUrl: 小白兔的眼睛为什么是红的.jpg

title.en: Why Don’t Polar Bears Feel Cold?

content.zh: 北极熊的毛是中空的，能存住空气保暖；皮肤是黑的，能吸住太阳的热；皮下还有厚厚一层脂肪，像穿了三件棉袄。
content.en: A polar bear’s hollow hairs trap warm air, its black skin soaks up the sun’s heat, and a thick layer of fat lies underneath — like wearing three coats.

title.zh: 猫为什么爱吃鱼和老鼠
title.en: Why Do Cats Love Fish and Mice?

content.zh: 猫的身体自己造不出一种叫牛磺酸的东西，而鱼和老鼠里正好有很多。不吃它，猫的眼睛和心脏就会出问题。
content.en: Cats cannot make a substance called taurine, which fish and mice contain plenty of. Without it, a cat’s eyes and heart suffer.

title.en: Why Do Cows Keep Chewing?

content.zh: 牛吃草时先匆忙吞下去，休息时再把草吐回嘴里慢慢嚼碎，这叫反刍。它有四个胃，要把草嚼得很细才好消化。
content.en: Cattle swallow grass in a hurry, then bring it back up to chew slowly while resting. This is chewing the cud. Their four stomachs need grass chewed very fine.

title.en: Why Do Horses Sleep Standing Up?

content.zh: 马的祖先在草原上要随时防备野兽，站着能一有动静就跑。马腿上有个"卡扣"，站着不用花力气也能站稳睡着。
content.en: Wild horses had to watch for predators, and standing let them run at once. A locking joint in their legs lets them doze upright without effort.

title.en: Why Do Crabs Walk Sideways?

content.zh: 螃蟹的腿关节只能上下弯，不能前后弯，所以只能横着迈。横着走还方便它扁平的身体贴着石头缝钻来钻去。
content.en: A crab’s leg joints bend up and down, not forwards, so it can only walk sideways. Sideways walking also suits its flat body squeezing through rock gaps.

title.en: Why Does a Peacock Spread Its Tail?

content.zh: 开屏的是公孔雀。它把尾羽张成一把大扇子，是在向母孔雀炫耀自己有多健康、多强壮，好让对方选中它。
content.en: It is the male that fans his tail, showing off how healthy and strong he is so that a female will choose him.

title.en: Why Do Geese Fly in a Line?

content.zh: 前面的大雁扇翅膀会带起一股上升的气流，后面的借着这股气流飞，能省很多力气。排队还能互相照应不掉队。
content.en: Each bird’s wings make an updraft that the one behind can ride, saving energy. Flying in a line also keeps the flock together.

title.en: Why Do Fireflies Glow?

content.zh: 萤火虫肚子末端有一种发光的东西，和空气里的氧一碰就亮起来，而且几乎不发热。它们用一闪一闪的光来找同伴。
content.en: A light-producing substance at the tip of its abdomen glows when it meets oxygen, giving off almost no heat. Fireflies flash to find one another.

title.en: Why Do Dragonflies Touch the Water?

content.zh: 蜻蜓点水是在产卵。它用尾巴轻轻碰一下水面，把卵产在水里。孵出来的小蜻蜓住在水中，要过很久才飞上天。
content.en: Dragonflies touch the water to lay eggs, dipping the tip of the tail onto the surface. The young hatch and live underwater for a long time before flying.

title.zh: 骆驼的驼峰里装的是什么
title.en: What Is Inside a Camel’s Hump?

content.zh: 驼峰里装的不是水，是一大块脂肪。找不到食物时，骆驼就慢慢消耗这些脂肪顶饿，好几天不吃也能赶路。
content.en: A camel’s hump holds fat, not water. When food is scarce the camel lives off this fat, and can travel for days without eating.

title.en: Why Do Chameleons Change Colour?

content.zh: 变色龙的皮肤里有许多小晶体，它把皮肤一松一紧，晶体排列变了，反射的光就变了颜色。变色还能表达害怕或生气。
content.en: A chameleon’s skin holds tiny crystals. By loosening or tightening the skin it changes how they line up, altering the light reflected. Colours also show fear or anger.

title.zh: 蝙蝠为什么倒挂着睡觉
title.en: Why Do Bats Sleep Upside Down?

content.zh: 蝙蝠的翅膀不适合助跑起飞，倒挂着松爪一落就能飞走。而且高处天敌少，睡着也安全。
content.en: Bat wings cannot launch from the ground, so hanging lets them simply let go and fly. High places are also safer from predators.

title.zh: 大象的长鼻子有什么用
title.en: What Is an Elephant's Trunk For?

content.zh: 象鼻是鼻子和上唇长成的，既能呼吸、闻味，又能卷起草、吸水和洗澡，顶端的小指还能捏起一粒花生。
content.en: A trunk is a long nose and upper lip. It breathes, smells, pulls up grass, sucks water for drinking and bathing, and its tip can pick up a single peanut.

title.zh: 长颈鹿的脖子为什么那么长
title.en: Why Do Giraffes Have Such Long Necks?

content.zh: 长脖子能吃到别的动物够不着的树叶，站得高还看得远，容易发现远处的狮子。脖子太长也给喝水带来麻烦。
content.en: A long neck reaches leaves no other animal can get, and it gives a fine view to spot lions far away. The downside is that drinking is awkward.

title.en: Why Do Kangaroos Have a Pouch?

content.zh: 袋鼠宝宝出生时只有花生米那么大，得爬进妈妈的育儿袋里喝奶、长大，长结实了才出来活动。
content.en: A newborn joey is only the size of a peanut. It crawls into the pouch to drink milk and grow, and comes out only when it is strong enough.

title.en: Why Don't Penguins Feel the Cold?

content.zh: 企鹅有厚厚的脂肪，羽毛又密又油还能防水；它们还会挤成一团互相取暖，外面冷，里面暖和。
content.en: Penguins carry thick fat and dense oily feathers that shed water. They also huddle together, so the outside of the group is cold while the middle stays warm.

title.en: What Does a Wagging Tail Mean?

content.zh: 狗用尾巴说话：摇得又快又松是开心，尾巴夹起来是害怕，竖着慢慢摆是在警惕。要看摇法才知道。
content.en: Dogs talk with their tails: a fast loose wag means happy, a tucked tail means scared, and a slow stiff one means watch out. How it moves tells you the mood.

title.en: What Is the Bee Dance Saying?

content.zh: 找到花的蜜蜂回巢会跳“8”字舞，跳舞的方向和时长告诉大家花在哪个方向、有多远。
content.en: A bee that finds flowers dances a figure of eight back home. The angle and length of the dance tell the others which way to fly and how far.

title.zh: 蚂蚁为什么会排着队走
title.en: Why Do Ants Walk in a Line?

content.zh: 走过路的蚂蚁会留下气味，后面的同伴闻着气味跟上，队伍就越排越长，像一条看不见的路标。
content.en: Ants leave a scent trail as they walk. Others follow the smell, and soon a long line forms along an invisible path.

title.zh: 蜘蛛为什么不会被自己的网粘住
title.en: Why Doesn't a Spider Stick to Its Own Web?

content.zh: 蛛网只有一部分丝是黏的，蜘蛛专挑干丝走；它脚上还有油和细毛，踩到黏丝也能轻松抬起来。
content.en: Only some threads of a web are sticky, and spiders step on the dry ones. Oily hairs on their feet also help them lift off cleanly.

title.en: Why Do Snakes Shed Their Skin?

content.zh: 蛇的皮肤不会跟着身体长大，长到一定程度就得换掉。旧皮从嘴边开始裂开，蛇一点点把它蹭下来。
content.en: Snake skin cannot grow with the body, so it must be replaced. The old skin splits at the mouth and the snake rubs it off bit by bit.

title.en: Why Does a Squid Squirt Ink?

content.zh: 遇到危险时乌贼喷出一团黑墨，把水搅浑。趁敌人看不清，它自己早就溜走了。
content.en: In danger a squid releases a cloud of black ink that clouds the water. While the enemy cannot see, the squid slips away.

title.en: Why Do Fish Sleep with Eyes Open?

content.zh: 大多数鱼没有眼皮，想闭也闭不上。它们睡觉时只是躲在水草或石头后一动不动，慢慢休息。
content.en: Most fish have no eyelids, so they cannot shut them. When resting they simply hide among plants or rocks and stay very still.

title.zh: 猫头鹰为什么晚上才出来
title.en: Why Do Owls Come Out at Night?

content.zh: 猫头鹰的眼睛在暗处特别灵敏，耳朵还能听出最轻的响动，翅膀又软又静。夜里老鼠多，正好开饭。
content.en: Owls see well in the dark, hear the faintest rustle and fly on silent wings, and night is when the mice are about.

title.zh: 啄木鸟为什么不停地啄树
title.en: Why Does a Woodpecker Peck All Day?

content.zh: 它在树皮下面找虫子，也用啄声告诉同伴这是自己的地盘，有时还啄出洞来筑巢。
content.en: It is hunting grubs under the bark, telling rivals the tree is taken, and sometimes carving out a nest hole.

title.en: Why Can Parrots Talk?

content.zh: 鹦鹉的舌头又厚又灵活，大脑里还有专门学声音的区域。它们模仿听到的声音，并不是真的懂意思。
content.en: A parrot has a thick, nimble tongue and a brain area for learning sounds, so it copies what it hears without knowing the meaning.

title.zh: 燕子为什么要飞到南方
title.en: Why Do Swallows Fly South?

content.zh: 冬天北方虫子躲起来了，燕子没东西吃，只好飞到暖和的南方。等春天虫子多了，它们再飞回来。
content.en: In winter the insects up north disappear, so swallows fly to warmer places, returning in spring when food is plentiful again.

title.en: Why Do Cranes Stand on One Leg?

content.zh: 把一只脚收进羽毛里能少散掉不少热，站着也更省力。它们还会左右换脚，轮流休息。
content.en: Tucking one leg into the feathers saves a lot of body heat and takes less effort, and they swap legs to give each a rest.

title.en: Why Can't Ostriches Fly?

content.zh: 鸵鸟太重了，翅膀撑不起来，胸骨上也没有飞鸟那块挂肌肉的龙骨。但它跑起来能到 70 公里。
content.en: Ostriches are far too heavy for their wings, and their breastbone lacks the ridge flying birds use, but they can run at 70 km/h.

title.en: Why Do Ducks Swim So Well?

content.zh: 鸭子的脚上有蹼，一划能推很多水；羽毛上还有油，水进不去，身子又轻又暖。
content.en: Webbed feet push a lot of water with each stroke, and oily feathers keep water out, leaving the bird light and warm.

title.en: Why Do Frogs Hibernate?

content.zh: 天冷时虫子没了，青蛙体温跟着降，就钻进泥底睡觉，靠皮肤呼吸熬过冬天，春天再出来。
content.en: With no insects about in the cold, a frog slows down and buries itself in mud, breathing through its skin until spring.

title.zh: 毛毛虫是怎么变成蝴蝶的
title.en: How Does a Caterpillar Become a Butterfly?

content.zh: 毛毛虫吃够叶子后结成蛹，在蛹里身体几乎化成液体，再重新长成有翅膀的蝴蝶，这叫完全变态。
content.en: After eating its fill the caterpillar forms a chrysalis, where the body almost liquefies and rebuilds into a winged butterfly, a change called metamorphosis.

title.en: Why Do Cicadas Shed Their Skin?

content.zh: 蝉的外壳不会长大，身体长大就得换掉。它从背上裂开爬出来，留下一个完整的空壳挂在树上。
content.en: A cicada's shell cannot grow, so it must be replaced, and the insect splits the back and climbs out, leaving an empty case on the tree.

title.en: What Are a Ladybird's Spots For?

content.zh: 鲜艳的红色和黑点是在警告：我不好吃。鸟啄过一次记住了，下次就不敢再碰它。
content.en: The bright red and black warn that it tastes foul, and a bird that tries once remembers and leaves them alone afterwards.

title.en: How Many Legs Does a Centipede Have?

content.zh: 名字叫百足，其实腿从十几对到一百多对不等，而且总是奇数对。腿数随种类不同，没有固定答案。
content.en: Despite the name the legs range from a dozen pairs to over a hundred, always an odd number of pairs, and it varies by species.

title.en: Why Does a Snail Carry a Shell?

content.zh: 壳是它随身的家：柔软的身体缩进去就安全了，还能挡住干燥。壳跟着身体一起长大。
content.en: The shell is a house it carries, a safe place to pull its soft body into and a shield against drying out, and it grows along with the snail.

title.en: Why Do Earthworms Burrow?

content.zh: 它们在土里吃腐烂的叶子，一路钻出通道，让空气和水进到土里，顺手把土翻松，是田地的好帮手。
content.en: They eat rotting leaves underground, and their tunnels let air and water in while loosening the soil, making them a farmer's helper.

title.en: Why Don't Ants Get Lost?

content.zh: 蚂蚁一路留下气味，回来照着走；有的还靠太阳的角度和步数定位，几种办法一起用。
content.en: Ants leave a scent trail to follow home, and some also use the sun's angle and count their steps, combining several methods.

title.en: Why Do Lions Roar?

content.zh: 吼声能传出几公里，用来告诉别的狮群这是我的地盘，也方便同伴在黑暗里找到彼此。
content.en: A roar carries for kilometres, telling other prides this territory is taken and helping the pride find one another in the dark.

title.zh: 老虎身上的条纹有什么用
title.en: What Are a Tiger's Stripes For?

content.zh: 条纹能把老虎的轮廓打碎，混在草丛和树影里不容易被看出。每只老虎的花纹都不一样，像指纹。
content.en: Stripes break up the tiger's outline so it melts into grass and shadow, and no two tigers share the same pattern, much like fingerprints.

title.en: Why Do Zebras Have Stripes?

content.zh: 科学家认为条纹能赶走爱叮它们的苍蝇，也能让狮子在奔跑的群体里看不清单只斑马。
content.en: Scientists think the stripes put off biting flies and make it hard for a lion to pick out one zebra from a running herd.

title.zh: 犀牛的角是干什么用的
title.en: What Is a Rhino's Horn For?

content.zh: 角用来在打斗中自卫、在泥地里刨食，也能拨开挡路的树枝。它不是骨头，是压紧的角质。
content.en: The horn serves in fights, for digging in mud and pushing aside branches, and it is not bone but tightly packed keratin.

title.zh: 河马为什么老待在水里
title.en: Why Do Hippos Stay in Water?

content.zh: 河马皮肤很薄，离水久了会干裂。泡在水里既防晒又凉快，晚上才上岸找吃的。
content.en: Their thin skin cracks if it dries out, so water keeps them cool and protected from the sun, and they graze on land only at night.

title.zh: 猴子为什么互相整理毛
title.en: Why Do Monkeys Groom Each Other?

content.zh: 互相捉虱子是清洁，更是交朋友：花时间给对方理毛，关系就亲近，吵架后也用它和解。
content.en: Grooming cleans the fur but mostly builds friendships, since time spent on someone strengthens the bond and helps make up after a fight.

title.en: Why Do Bears Sleep Through Winter?

content.zh: 冬天食物稀少，熊就躲进洞里，靠秋天攒下的脂肪过活，心跳和体温都降下来，这叫冬眠。
content.en: With little food in winter a bear dens up and lives on fat stored in autumn, slowing its heart and cooling its body in hibernation.

title.zh: 松鼠为什么把果子埋起来
title.en: Why Do Squirrels Bury Nuts?

content.zh: 松鼠把吃不完的坚果藏在各处，冬天再挖出来。有些被忘掉的就发了芽，等于帮树播了种。
content.en: Squirrels hide nuts they cannot eat at once and dig them up in winter, and the ones they forget sprout, planting new trees.

title.en: Why Is a Hedgehog Covered in Spines?

content.zh: 刺是改装过的毛。遇到危险它缩成一团，把刺全部竖起来，狐狸和狗就无从下嘴。
content.en: The spines are modified hairs, and when danger comes it rolls into a ball with every spine raised, leaving a fox no way to bite.

title.en: Why Do Cats Like to Scratch?

content.zh: 抓挠能把旧爪鞘磨掉、让爪子保持锋利，也是伸懒腰。抓痕和气味还在告诉别的猫这是我的地盘。
content.en: Scratching sheds the old claw sheath and keeps claws sharp, it stretches the body, and the marks and scent claim the place as theirs.

title.en: Why Do Dogs Sniff Everywhere?

content.zh: 狗的嗅觉比人强几万倍。闻一闻就知道谁来过、心情怎么样，这是它们读新闻的方式。
content.en: A dog's nose is tens of thousands of times better than ours, and sniffing tells who passed by and how they felt, which is how dogs read the news.

title.zh: 兔子的耳朵为什么那么长
title.en: Why Do Rabbits Have Such Long Ears?

content.zh: 长耳朵能收集很远的细微声音，早早发现危险；耳朵上血管多，天热时还能帮忙散热。
content.en: Long ears pick up faint sounds from far away to spot danger early, and their many blood vessels help shed heat when it is warm.

title.en: Why Do Rodents Always Gnaw?

content.zh: 老鼠的门牙一辈子都在长，不磨就会越长越长伤到自己，所以它们要不停啃硬东西。
content.en: Their front teeth grow all their lives, and without constant gnawing they would grow too long and cause harm, so they chew hard things.

title.en: How Do Birds Fly?

content.zh: 鸟的骨头是空心的，很轻；翅膀上面鼓下面平，扇动时产生升力；羽毛还能减少阻力。
content.en: Bird bones are hollow and light, the curved wing makes lift as it flaps, and feathers smooth the air flowing past.

title.zh: 小鸟站在电线上为什么不会触电
title.en: Why Don't Birds on a Wire Get Shocked?

content.zh: 它两只脚都站在同一根电线上，身体里没有高低电压差，电流就不流过它。碰到另一根线才会出事。
content.en: Both feet rest on the same wire, so there is no voltage difference across its body and no current flows, and only touching another wire would be fatal.

title.en: Why Can't Chickens Fly High?

content.zh: 家鸡被人类养了几千年，翅膀退化、身体变重，只能扑腾几下飞过矮墙，飞不了远路。
content.en: Kept by people for thousands of years, domestic chickens have weak wings and heavy bodies, managing only a short flutter over a low wall.

title.zh: 企鹅走路为什么摇摇摆摆
title.en: Why Do Penguins Waddle?

content.zh: 企鹅的腿又短又靠后，身子又圆又重。左右摇摆能省力气，比迈大步更稳当，冰面也不容易滑倒。
content.en: With short legs set far back and a round heavy body, they rock from side to side, which saves effort and keeps them steady on ice.

title.en: What Are Animal Tails For?

content.zh: 尾巴用处多：猴子拿它当第五只手，鳄鱼用它游泳，牛拿它赶苍蝇，松鼠冬天把它当被子。
content.en: Tails do many jobs: a monkey uses one as a fifth hand, a crocodile swims with it, cattle swat flies, and a squirrel wraps it up as a blanket.

title.zh: 动物为什么要成群生活
title.en: Why Do Animals Live in Groups?

content.zh: 一群里眼睛多，容易发现敌人；一起捕猎也更省力。虽然要分食物，但换来的是安全。
content.en: Many eyes spot danger sooner and hunting together costs less effort, so sharing food is worth the safety a group brings.

title.en: How Do Animals Survive Winter?

content.zh: 办法各不相同：有的冬眠，有的换上厚毛，有的迁徙到南方，还有的靠秋天存下的食物过活。
content.en: Ways differ: some hibernate, some grow thick fur, some migrate south, and others live on food stored during autumn.

title.zh: 为什么有的动物会装死
title.en: Why Do Some Animals Play Dead?

content.zh: 不少捕食者只追活物，装死能让对方失去兴趣；有的还会放出臭味配合演出等敌人走开。
content.en: Many hunters only chase live prey, so playing dead puts them off, and some even give off a bad smell to complete the act.
